title: flow designer: renaming a node in the inspector's ID field leaves its edges naming the old id, so the renamed node is disconnected
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect, class (a), a wrong result at a public entry point: the Studio flow inspector's node ID field. Measured on the real component. Reader: objectui triage first-touch (grade and route).
Dedupe (MCP `search_issues`, objectui, open + closed):
- "flow designer node id rename in inspector leaves edges pointing at old id, renamed node disconnected" gave 5 hits. objectui#11772 (the same family, below) and objectui#11778 (the add-node paths) are open; objectui#10948, #11085 and #6287 are closed. None covers renaming.
- Positive control: "flow designer remove node leaves dangling edges reused node id re-attaches" returned objectui#11772.

Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat 3 (`session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8`) from the objectui#11772 dev report (`6043897905`, out-of-scope finding 1). ⛔ Not graded or routed here; ⛔ not a claim.

## What happens

`FlowNodeInspector`'s ID field (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/FlowNodeInspector.tsx:461` on `9990f9e`) commits `patchNode({ id: v })`. The patch carries only `nodes`. Every edge whose `source` or `target` named the old id keeps naming it.

Measured by the objectui#11772 dev with a throwaway probe on that card's branch. In a flow with edges `s → x` and `x → e`, `fireEvent.change` on the ID field from `x` to `renamed` committed a patch whose `edges` was `undefined`. The renamed node is left with no edges, and both edges name a node that no longer exists. The dev also reports that the field commits on every keystroke, so each intermediate spelling is a rename.

What objectui#11772 (PR objectui#11825) changes and does not change here:
- the old id is never minted again within the session, so a later node cannot silently inherit the edges;
- the Problems panel's existing `edgeSourceMissing` / `edgeTargetMissing` rows name the dangling edges;
- the edges still do not follow the rename.

The engine executes a flow's edges as stored. A published flow whose node was renamed in Studio therefore never runs that node, unless objectstack-ai/objectstack#22088's server-side refusal lands first and refuses the publish.

Same family as objectui#11772: designer writes leave edges naming a node that does not exist.

## Done when

- Renaming a node's id rewrites every edge endpoint that named it, in the same patch, and a rename can never join a half-typed id to another node's edges, for example because it commits on blur or refuses a collision. The claimant picks and names the design.
- Pins:
  - rename `x` → `renamed` in a flow `s → x → e`: both edges follow, and nothing dangles;
  - a rename to an id another node already has is refused or never committed;
  - control: editing any other node field leaves `edges` untouched.

Dedupe words: flow node id rename edges dangling · inspector id field edges not renamed · renamed node disconnected
